reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight of the thesis lies in the formulation of a generative probabilistic model for event discovery from video. This model leverages relational spatio-temporal graphs to encode qualitative spatial and temporal relationships among objects and events. The unsupervised nature of the approach allows for automatic identification of event classes without manual labeling, enabling scalability to real-world video domains. The derivation proceeds from defining a likelihood function over spatio-temporal graphs, followed by variational inference to approximate posterior distributions over event classes. Dualities emerge in how the model treats events as both objects and processes—where object identities are inferred through their roles within event structures. Failure modes arise when spatial or temporal coherence is insufficient, leading to fragmented or misclassified event graphs. The mathematical framework supports robustness through graph-based regularization and probabilistic consistency checks.
